text:
sam: Hey team — customer HealthBridge reporting truncated SSE outputs when their client reconnects after a short network blip. They see a valid stream for ~95% of requests but ~5% end with an incomplete JSON and no finish_reason.

sam: Example from their capture: final chunk looks like this (cut mid-object):

```
data: {\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"...\"},\"index\":0,\"finish_reason\":
```

sam: So the last token and finish_reason are missing — parse errors on their side. Happening during reconnect/resume.

ryan: Thanks, Sam. Any reproducible steps from HealthBridge?

sam: They provided a minimal repro: long-ish generation (~900 tokens) + intentionally drop connection at ~85% via client-side abort, then client reconnects with resume headers. Repro command they used:

```
curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \
  \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=longgen&resume=true&session=hb-1337\"
```

sam: When they reconnect, server resumes but final event sometimes never reaches client (connection closes without terminal JSON).

lisa: Do they hit any rate limits or auth rotations during the cycle? Could be an auth handoff dropping trailing bytes.

sam: They say no — token stable for test. Also tried with keepalive pings disabled. Same behavior.

jordan: Can you paste a raw TCP capture or proxy logs? We need to know where bytes are lost: at LB/proxy vs runtime.

sam: Pasting their HTTP proxy logs snippet:

```
[2026-02-15T14:03:21Z] upstream 200 chunked
[2026-02-15T14:03:22Z] client disconnect after 0.12s (reconnect)
[2026-02-15T14:03:22Z] backend reattach id=hb-1337 resume
[2026-02-15T14:03:22Z] upstream close without FIN
```

sam: They also attached the runtime trace (sanitized):

```
2026-02-15T14:03:21.300 INFO allocate worker w-11 session=hb-1337
2026-02-15T14:03:21.900 INFO emit chunk seq=184 session=hb-1337
2026-02-15T14:03:22.150 INFO reattach resume session=hb-1337
2026-02-15T14:03:22.420 WARN client connection closed before final chunk
```

jordan: Preliminary hypothesis: LB or proxy (nginx/fastly) is aggressively closing the socket during a quick reattach, swallowing the last TCP segments from runtime. That leaves the client with truncated stream. The runtime logged the final emit but the upstream close happened before bytes flushed to client.

lisa: Could also be TLS session renegotiation or HTTP/2 stream reset on our edge. Do they use HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2?

sam: HealthBridge test used HTTP/2 (browser client). They reproduced from a server-side test harness as well (netcat style) with similar results.

jordan: Steps I'll take:
- Ask infra to check LB config for proxy_buffering and tcp_nodelay semantics on resume.
- Add extra flush/linger routine to runtime after emitting final chunk when resume header is present (temporary).
- Request tcpdump from customer for the failing window.

lisa: I'll check edge logs around that time for RST/GOAWAY, buffering config, and whether edge truncated because of backpressure. Possible mitigation: bump keepalive and add a short drain delay on reattach path.

ryan: Sam — please get the HealthBridge tcpdump + a HAR of the failed request. Also ask them to try with explicit HTTP/1.1 to rule out h2 reset semantics.

sam: Done. Customer uploaded pcap link and confirmed H1 test: H1 still shows missing final bytes but less frequent. They also noted this happens more under bursty traffic (backpressure).

jordan: That points to a race under backpressure: runtime emits final JSON, signals upstream, but edge/transport closes connection while some TLS/TCP segments are still queued. I'll instrument runtime to log post-flush confirmation and add a short 200ms linger to ensure socket drain. Will open an eng-runtime PR and a mitigative guard in edge config.

lisa: If we change edge config, we need to coordinate with infra to rollout to prod slowly (canary). I'll prepare a checklist.

ryan: Tagging support ticket TKT-4721 on the case and adding HealthBridge contact.

sam: Assigning owners: jordan -> eng-runtime (investigate + PR), lisa -> eng-infra (edge buffering + logs), ryan -> support (customer comms + pcap).

jordan: Will try to reproduce locally with a script that simulates client abort + immediate reconnect under a proxy that simulates backpressure. If I can reproduce, I'll attach a gdb trace and post a small failing repro.

sam: Customer appreciated quick triage. They've paused production traffic until we confirm a fix.

lisa: FYI, I found a recent edge change that tightened socket timeouts during burst to reduce resource usage — reverting that might reduce failures while we ship the runtime change.

jordan: Plan: short-term revert edge timeout (canary), medium-term runtime linger flush + post-emit ack, long-term protocol-level resume handshake to confirm terminal event delivery.

sam: Thanks. I'll update the HealthBridge thread with the plan and ETA. Closing loop here once infra can confirm the canary revert. :thumbsup:

healthbridge-bot: Uploaded pcap to https://storage.healthbridge.example/pcaps/hb-1337.pcap (access granted to redwood-support).

sam: Got it — thanks.

ryan: Marking this thread as escalated to eng-runtime + eng-infra.

jordan: Adding note: watch for missing finish_reason and incomplete JSON in logs as signal for this bug (rare but high-impact).

sam: End of thread for now.
